memoryTip: Like a tally stick of marks — counts match / add up.
correctPassage: The final vote tally confirmed that the amendment had failed by a narrow margin.
wrongPassages: The machine ran tally until the breaker tripped from sustained overload.
The team shipped tally by skipping every checklist item on the release gate.
He negotiated tally by accepting the first offer without a counter.

memoryTip: Like a dusty nebula — cloudy, vague, not sharply defined.
correctPassage: Critics called the mission statement nebulous because it never defined success.
wrongPassages: The engineer’s nebulous blueprint specified every measurement to the millimeter.
After the numbered checklist, nobody found the steps nebulous—each had a diagram.
She stored the nebulous in a jar beside the other solid lab samples.

memoryTip: Doesn’t assume airs — quiet and modest.
correctPassage: Despite her fame, she remained unassuming and preferred to work without publicity.
wrongPassages: The ice lip felt unassuming on a grated overlook with warning signs.
He ranked the obstacle unassuming after walking around it in ten seconds.
The crevasse hop felt unassuming on a seasonal bridge with rails.

memoryTip: Out + size — bigger than the usual size.
correctPassage: The museum devoted an outsize share of its budget to a single traveling exhibit.
wrongPassages: They hoped to outsize the protest by moving public comment after midnight.
He moved to outsize the deposition by reading a prepared statement for every answer.
He tried to outsize the gag by quoting “anonymous sources” that were himself.

memoryTip: In-extricable: can’t extract yourself — tangled tight.
correctPassage: In the novel, personal loyalty and political ambition become inextricable.
wrongPassages: He greened the PIR checklist as inextricable with owners still unassigned.
an inextricable integration test mocks every dependency, including the system under test.
Her inextricable sketch caught the likeness in a few decisive lines.

definition: not in harmony; out of place
memoryTip: In-congruent: doesn’t “fit” the picture; out of place.
correctPassage: A neon sign looked incongruous against the centuries-old stone facade.
wrongPassages: Critics called the clean version incongruous for removing the song’s only edge.
Parents called the concert incongruous after every child sat still through two full hours.
Her incongruous printer’s note described a binding that was never used.

memoryTip: Im-pertinent: not “pertaining” politely — rude and out of line.
correctPassage: The reporter’s impertinent questions about private finances angered the candidate.
wrongPassages: The ice tongue tip felt impertinent behind a fence and viewing platform.
The leading-tone held was impertinent under a final open fifth on I.
The wharf’s impertinent bollard load plate was for gear never installed on site.

memoryTip: Can’t surmount (climb over) it — too big a barrier.
correctPassage: What had seemed an insurmountable funding gap was closed by a single anonymous gift.
wrongPassages: The approach felt insurmountable on a catwalk with welded railings.
The stand looked insurmountable in rain with awnings still rolled up.
The trail was so insurmountable that first-time hikers finished early without maps or guides.

definition: the quality of being calm and peaceful
memoryTip: Tranquil + ity — calm lake, quiet mind.
correctPassage: After the storm, a rare sense of tranquility settled over the harbor.
wrongPassages: He matched zero locks with the keys from drawer tranquility.
He titled a sticky note tranquility and stuck it on an empty monitor.
The door system ignored middle initial tranquility after a firmware update.

definition: a temporary relief from something unpleasant
memoryTip: A brief relief before the “hard thing” resumes — temporary break.
correctPassage: A last-minute injunction granted the tenants a temporary reprieve from eviction.
wrongPassages: The cattle dock looked reprieve with ramps chained and unused for years.
The clinic tried to reprieve no-shows by double-booking every appointment slot.
The explosion hatch was reprieve and never opened in the overpressure test.

definition: not allowing passage; unable to be affected
memoryTip: Im-pervious: nothing can pierce through (water, criticism).
correctPassage: The coating is nearly impervious to water and salt air.
wrongPassages: The queue tried to impervious ASA by answering and parking callers on mute.
The trail felt impervious under boardwalk that never touched the mud.
The thermal fuse was impervious and never opened in the oven test.

definition: not able to be defended or maintained
memoryTip: Can’t “tenably” hold it — argument collapses; position is indefensible.
correctPassage: Once the data were corrected, the original hypothesis became untenable.
wrongPassages: The countersubject was untenable and never entered stretto.
The crowd noise was untenable after the engineer isolated a single clap.
She treated the requirement as untenable after the client waived it in writing.

memoryTip: Ubi = where (Latin) — seems to be everywhere you look.
correctPassage: Smartphones are now so ubiquitous that many public spaces assume constant connectivity.
wrongPassages: Rotary phones are ubiquitous here: one sits on every modern classroom desk.
The orchid is ubiquitous—only a single wild specimen has ever been found.
He kept his ubiquitous diary in one locked drawer no visitor ever saw.

memoryTip: De-funct: function stopped — dead, no longer running.
correctPassage: The defunct railway line has been converted into a walking path.
wrongPassages: He marked maintenance defunct while the change window still ran long.
a defunct golden test compares two empty files and passes.
The migration looked defunct on radar: one dense flock on a straight line.

memoryTip: De-tract: pulls reputation down — a critic who knocks you.
correctPassage: Even the project’s fiercest detractor admitted the design was elegant.
wrongPassages: She emptied folder detractor and it still showed 1 item: thumbs.db.
He stamped detractor in gold on an one-page “permit” of doodles.
He wore the detractor ribbon upside down as a joke name tag.

memoryTip: Exhausts every option — complete, thorough, nothing left out.
correctPassage: An exhaustive review of the literature found no support for the claim.
wrongPassages: Critics called the box-set transfer exhaustive for surface noise left uncleaned.
The reedbed pool stayed exhaustive after a cut-off channel bypassed it entirely.
Viewers found the HDR pass exhaustive for crushing all shadow detail.

memoryTip: Hetero = different — a mixed, diverse group.
correctPassage: The sample was deliberately heterogeneous, including rural and urban schools.
wrongPassages: Fans found the immersive mix heterogeneous for burying the lead vocal.
The walk felt heterogeneous on a paved ramp with continuous handrails.
The salt pan stayed heterogeneous under a water budget with no wet season.

memoryTip: Like an imperative sentence (command) — must-do, essential.
correctPassage: With the storm approaching, it was imperative that residents evacuate promptly.
wrongPassages: The bay stand looked imperative between waves of arriving coaches.
The river ran imperative once engineers replaced every bend with a straight channel.
The bureau hoped to imperative backlog age by resetting ticket clocks nightly.

definition: a subtle difference in meaning or expression
memoryTip: New-ance of meaning — a subtle shade, not black-and-white.
correctPassage: The translation preserved every nuance of the original poem’s tone.
wrongPassages: The hard looked nuance between markets with trestles stacked aside.
Her nuance bibliography cited URLs that only returned 404 errors.
The timber dock looked nuance at low water with piles fully exposed.

memoryTip: Causes controversy — people argue about it.
correctPassage: The museum’s controversial exhibit drew both praise and protests.
wrongPassages: The wetland stayed controversial in plans that banned any new fill.
The thermal link was controversial: it held past the oven’s maximum temperature.
Boards postponed the controversial safety retrofit inspectors had required.
